messages:
mila: Trying the VS Code quickstart (the new Extension) and the "first call" from the WebView fails with a CORS preflight error, but when I run curl I get a billing_required JSON. Very confusing for users in the editor.
ron: Hmm, is the extension making the request from the renderer (WebView) or via the extension host (node)? Browser contexts enforce CORS and can hide the real server response.
mila: It's a WebView that loads the sample app html and does fetch() to https://api.play.redwood.ai/v1/generate. Dev console shows: 
```
Access to fetch at 'https://api.play.redwood.ai/v1/generate' from origin 'vscode-webview://extension.id' has been blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present on the requested resource.
```
jess: That explains the CORS. The server is not serving CORS headers for editor WebViews (we don't allow arbitrary origins). But why does curl show billing_required?
ron: Two separate things: 1) WebView blocked by CORS before the response body is exposed, so the extension user sees a generic network/CORS error. 2) When you run curl directly (outside WebView), you can see the backend's JSON which indicates billing gating. So users get a frontend-only error in the editor which doesn't hint at billing.
mila: Repro steps: open extension, click "Run quickstart", extension loads webview/sample.html -> fetch to /v1/generate -> console shows CORS error. Then I run in terminal: `curl -v https://api.play.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"` -> returns {"error":"billing_required","message":"workspace needs billing setup"}.
ops: Two action items: 1) Quickstart extension should perform network calls from the extension host (node) where CORS doesn't apply, or proxy via the native host. 2) Quickstart UX should detect common errors and show a friendly message: "Connectivity error — check billing and proxy" instead of raw CORS.
jess: Agreed. Also add a short note in the extension README: "If you see a CORS error in the WebView, run the quickstart from the extension host (Run in Terminal) or ensure your workspace has billing accepted."
ron: I'll open DEVEX-1160 to track changing the extension to use the extension host for first-call and to surface billing vs CORS clearly in the UI.
devex-bot: new issue created: DEVEX-1160 "vscode-extension: avoid WebView CORS for first-call & show explicit billing message"  assigned to ron
mila: For immediate workaround: open the Command Palette -> "Quickstart: Run in Terminal" or accept the org trial in the console. That fixed it for me.
jess: I pushed a tiny PR that changes the sample to call via the extension host when the extension detects a webview origin. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart/pull/70
ops: We'll also add a small telemetry event to track how many first-call failures in the extension are CORS vs billing so we can prioritize. Closing after the PR merge.
mila: Thanks y'all, saved me a support ticket. :)
